outcome: type of surgical procedure (salpingo-oophorectomy, adnexal cystectomy, detorsion)
presence of severe necrosis of adnexal tissue
cohort: The study included patients who underwent surgical management for adnexal torsion, divided into acute (<=24 h), subacute (2 days), and chronic (>=3 days) categories based on symptom onset to surgery time, with 49 patients in the acute and 45 in the chronic adnexal torsion groups analyzed comparatively.
finding: Chronic adnexal torsion patients were significantly older, more frequently presented with isolated tubal torsion, less often required emergency surgery, and were associated with severe necrosis, extensive pelvic adhesion, and longer surgical duration compared to acute adnexal torsion cases.
